content_text: Many of these bull points are bear points. Neutral at best. Start with the deterministic vs probabilistic argument - it shows a complete lack of understanding of how models have evolved in the last 18 months and what harnesses & agentic systems do. Agents don't hallucinate your ledger, they call the same deterministic APIs humans do. The LLM orchestrates, the database computes. Deterministic workflows (and more importantly science) is getting solved by LLMs every day now. Fundamentally, nobody serious thinks LLMs replace the ERP in the next few years - that's a strawman of the bear case, which was never about SAP going to zero. The actual bear case: SAP is the definitive market leader in the most penetrated market in software, with >75% of growth coming from expansion/upsell/pricing - precisely the levers that get compressed in an AI world. Think about what SAP is worth as a 2% organic grower instead of an 8% LFL grower. Now the "toll road" argument: SAP already gets paid MILLIONS to host and organize its clients' data. Think about that - they get paid for hosting holding and organizing their customer's data - that's it. Charging them a second time for AI to access it isn't monetization - it's a hostage fee, and it's the exact playbook that triggered the indirect-access licensing revolt SAP had to walk back with Digital Access/DAAP 8 years ago. And if the moat outside of just "storing and organizing data" was real, why do you need gates at all? Fencing customers off from their own data is an admission the workflow layer is contestable. Also why SAP killed of @Celonis 5 years ago when they saw customers building away/on top of SAP (which could eventually be replaced by a $SNOW) - they panicked. The post is also contradictory: "SAP blocked external AI above ERP" and "Joule doesn't compete with other AI models" can't both be true. That's "we killed the competition" and "we have no competition" at the same time. FYI Joule being a wrapper on frontier models, SAP pays model COGS to its provider, so SAP is incentivized to slow roll this - but don't be fooled, both COGS and OPEX needs to go up if SAP is to succeed in its AI-world transition. Last one that made me giggle: the DCF "assumes zero AI monetization" but it also assumes zero AI cannibalization of the expansion/pricing engine. You don't get to add the option value but ignore the other side. $SAP
